original_draft.summary: The Black Shark T11 gaming earbuds are praised for their lightweight comfort (3.2 g), solid build, IPX4 water resistance, Bluetooth 5.3, 13 mm driver, and ultra-low latency gaming mode (source 54aca767, d21aa150). Battery life is consistently reported at up to 30 hours with the case (sources 2c91f666, 54aca767, 34d0451a). Sound quality is generally described as good with punchy bass (source 2c91f666) or immersive (source 34d0451a), though one reviewer finds bass only 'good but not great' and notes poor noise isolation due to the semi-in-ear design (source 2bb277ef). A key disagreement exists on gaming latency: while most sources report no perceptible lag (source d21aa150, 54aca767), one reviewer measured a ~0.1-second delay specifically in Free Fire (source 2bb277ef). Build quality is solid overall, but one source reports the sliding mechanism feels loose (source 2c91f666). The touch controls lack volume adjustment and single-tap response (source 2c91f666). Microphone quality is reported as poor (source 34d0451a). The earbuds are very affordable (139–169 AED, 399 MAD) and offer good value for budget-conscious gamers (sources d21aa150, 34d0451a).

empty_correction.summary: The Black Shark T11 is a budget gaming-oriented TWS earbud. One reviewer (source 2c91f666) reports solid build but a loose sliding mechanism, good sound with clean bass, clear directional audio in gaming mode, battery life of ~5 hours per charge (25-30 total), and a non-responsive single-tap touch sensor with no volume control. Another reviewer (source 2bb277ef) notes a ~0.1-second audio delay in Free Fire, bass described as 'good but not great', and poor noise isolation due to the semi-in-ear design. A third source (54aca767) lists manufacturer specs: 3.2 g weight, 30-hour total battery, Bluetooth 5.3, 13 mm driver, gaming mode, ENC call noise reduction, and IPX4 rating, but provides no verified testing. A fourth source (d21aa150) confirms ultra-low latency in PUBG, solid build, great sound, and a very cheap price (169 AED). A fifth source (34d0451a) reports light and comfortable fit, immersive sound, poor microphone quality, battery life exceeding 30 hours, and excellent value at 399 MAD. Key disagreements exist: build quality is called solid by some but the sliding mechanism is described as loose by one; latency is reported as non-existent by two sources but a 0.1-second delay is noted in Free Fire by another; sound quality is praised as immersive and great by some but only 'good not great' by another; and battery life claims vary from 25-30 hours tested to over 30 hours. The product lacks a companion app and volume controls, and has no ANC.
